definitions.gloss: to go to; to proceed to; to head for
definitions.explanation: To go to a place with a specific purpose, especially an important or formal destination. More literary and purposeful than simply 'to go.'

examples.japanese: {大臣|だいじん}は{被災地|ひさいち}に{赴|おもむ}いて{状況|じょうきょう}を{視察|しさつ}した。
examples.english: The minister went to the disaster area to inspect the situation.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{任地|にんち}に{赴|おもむ}くにあたって、{家族|かぞく}と{話|はな}し{合|あ}う{時間|じかん}を{設|もう}けた。
examples.english: Before heading to my new post, I made time to talk things over with my family.

notes:
{赴|おもむ}く is an intransitive godan verb. It is a formal, literary word meaning "to go" or "to proceed," implying a deliberate, purposeful journey.

ASPECT (ている):
{赴|おもむ}いている indicates a state of having gone to a place (resulting state).

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- Xに{赴|おもむ}く (go to X)
- Xへ{赴|おもむ}く (head toward X)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現場|げんば}に{赴|おもむ}く (go to the scene)
- {任地|にんち}に{赴|おもむ}く (go to one's assigned post)
- {戦地|せんち}に{赴|おもむ}く (go to the battlefield)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赴|おもむ}く vs {行|い}く: {赴|おもむ}く is formal and literary, implying purposeful travel to a specific destination, while {行|い}く is the everyday neutral word for going somewhere.
